clue.text: Endless pole, problem for marsupial

indicators.note: something without an end has lost its final part, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a post is an upright pole
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A pole that seems to go on for ever is causing trouble for some climbing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem' reads as part of the surface trouble, but it is an arithmetic sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A possum is a tree-dwelling pouched mammal of Australasia and the Americas, so it is a marsupial.

clue.text: Flag in shocking cold?

blocks.note: first meaning: a long narrow pennant flown from a mast
second meaning, playful: a cold that makes the nose run freely, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone is flagging, laid low by a terrible cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' reads as a verb meaning to tire, but it is the noun for a pennant; the second sense is a whimsical coinage for a cold with a constantly running nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long ribbon-like banner, and a bad cold that streams could jokingly be called one.

clue.text: Supersonic shifts in triangles etc

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Faster-than-sound movements happening in triangular formations, perhaps of aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a struck instrument, so triangles, drums and the like make up the percussion section.

clue.text: Look to break up wrong crowd — in which everyone joins in?

indicators.note: breaking something up means splitting it apart, so one word goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
a gang is a crowd or group
lo is an old word for look!

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out as someone sets about dispersing a bad lot of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look or behold; the crowd is split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A singalong is an informal gathering of shared singing, an event where all present take part.

clue.text: Piano sonata sounding terrific initially, listen!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words it follows

blocks.note: the heads of the four words in turn

explanation.surface: A piano sonata sounded wonderful from the start, so pay attention!
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissed interjection used to catch someone's attention quietly, much like saying hey or listen.

clue.text: Powerful words, something that may catch you stopping short

indicators.note: stopping before the end means the final letter is not reached

blocks.note: a mantrap is a trap set for people, especially trespassers

explanation.surface: Persuasive language can be a trap that catches you before you realise.
explanation.walkthrough: MANTRAP loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred chant or repeated formula believed to carry spiritual force.

clue.text: Might a low budget film be so dark?

definitions.text: Might a low budget film be so dark?

blocks.clueFragment: Might a low budget film be so dark?
blocks.note: surface reading: a cheap film with grim, gloomy content or poor lighting
setter's reading: a cheap film can't afford famous actors, and a night sky with no celestial lights is very dark

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark' suggests a gloomy tone or bad lighting, but the answer describes both a film lacking celebrities and a night sky with nothing shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Starless describes a night with no visible stars, and punningly a film with no star actors.

clue.text: Working, he got ridiculously busy

indicators.note: ridiculously means absurdly, so the preceding words are put into a silly new order

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
taken as written

explanation.surface: While at work he was absurdly busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go is an idiom for being active and constantly occupied.

clue.text: Partly provides for old poet

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the following word is used

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: Somewhat makes provision for an ageing versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet of the Augustan age, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Second isn't bad, crawler trailing behind

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so those letters are put out of order
trailing behind means following at the rear, so this piece is placed last

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
an ant is a crawling insect

explanation.surface: Coming second is no disgrace, says someone with a creep tagging along behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' suggests a toady, but it is just a small insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Second and instant are both nouns for a very brief moment, as in 'wait a second'.

clue.text: Croon about boat's artwork

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: to croon is to sing softly
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A singer warbles about the paintings on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketching is the making of rough drawings, so it can name a piece of art or the practice of producing it.

clue.text: Spud that's less hard: I'm not sure

indicators.note: less means minus, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
er is the hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone poking a potato wonders whether it has softened yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less hard' reads as softer, but it means remove the abbreviation for hard from the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tater and spud are both informal words for a potato.

clue.text: Mother, I nearly forgot disease!

blocks.note: mum is a British word for mother
a postscript adds what the writer nearly left out

explanation.surface: A child suddenly remembers to tell their mother about an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: PS stands for postscript, the line added at the end of a letter for something almost forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumps is a contagious viral illness causing swelling of the salivary glands.

clue.text: Alpine slipper concealing funny bags

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: a luge is a small sledge that slides down Alpine runs
a gag is a joke, something funny

explanation.surface: A skier's footwear hides amusing pouches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpine slipper' looks like indoor footwear but is something that slips down the slopes, a racing toboggan.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is the collective word for a traveller's bags and cases.

clue.text: Goalie after match revealed as worker on estate

blocks.note: a game is a match
a goalkeeper is called a keeper

explanation.surface: After the match, the goalkeeper turns out to have a job on a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the goalie's word behind the match word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamekeeper is employed on a country estate to breed and protect game birds and animals.

clue.text: Tiny crustacean: a few later cooked

indicators.note: cooked means mixed up and altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some small shellfish get boiled a bit afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A water flea, or daphnia, is a minute freshwater crustacean.

clue.text: One or two perhaps I'd written about in sexy book

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short word is read the other way
in places one piece inside another word

blocks.note: taken as written
carnal means sexual, of the flesh
Numbers is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone notes they've written an erotic book, maybe a couple of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is from the Old Testament; 'One or two' are examples of the definition, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: One and two are examples of counting numbers, which denote quantity rather than order.

clue.text: Fixed PC yet? Do I check text for errors?

indicators.note: fixed can mean rigged or rearranged, so the letters that follow are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the computer is repaired, and whether they should proofread.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy-edit is to prepare a manuscript for print by correcting mistakes in it.

clue.text: Digger once impressing a judge

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so one piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: a former miner, one who used to dig
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former excavator wows a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: EX- is the standard prefix for former, matching 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner assesses candidates, judging their work.

clue.text: Coppers perhaps welcoming any reduced punishment

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its last letter
welcoming means taking in, so one word holds another inside it

blocks.note: copper coins are pennies, plural pence
the word cut short

explanation.surface: Police officers might accept any lighter sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here it means copper coins, British pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment undertaken to atone for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Student finding feature of winter in autumn?

blocks.note: November is an autumn month, abbreviated
ice is typical of winter

explanation.surface: A pupil notices a wintry sign during the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a containment signal, but the month simply comes first and the wintry word follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a beginner or learner, so a student new to a subject.

clue.text: Rat pack member?

blocks.note: first meaning: a rogue, a dishonest scoundrel
second meaning: a court card in a pack of playing cards, the jack

explanation.walkthrough: The Rat Pack was the famous group of entertainers around Frank Sinatra, so the clue looks like it asks for one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is both a scoundrel and the old name for the jack in a deck of playing cards.

clue.text: Scalp important figure

indicators.note: scalping takes off the top, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: weighty means important or serious

explanation.surface: Take the top off a significant number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Important figure' looks like a VIP; the figure is a number alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighty is a number, and numbers are written as figures.

clue.text: Turkey dandy, left for stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so a letter is pushed inside the word

blocks.note: a fop is a vain dandy
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A fussy dresser leaves the stuffing for the Christmas turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' invites the roast bird, but it means a failure. L goes inside FOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is slang for a show or product that fails badly, which is a flop.

clue.text: Always hanging around Latvia's capital, slippery little thing

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so the opening letter is taken
hanging around means surrounding, so one word goes around the letter

blocks.note: ever means always
first letter of the country

explanation.surface: Something slimy forever loitering around Riga.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a small and famously slippery creature.

clue.text: Money to pay, ruined

blocks.note: first meaning: what a tenant pays to a landlord
second meaning: torn apart, ripped

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests being broke from bills; the second sense is the old past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the payment for using property, and also the past participle of rend, meaning torn.

clue.text: Uncertain if angler in a tangle having hooked boot in the end

indicators.note: a tangle is a muddle, so the letters are jumbled
the end points to the final letter of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fisherman snarled in his line, having landed an old boot, is unsure what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter T joins the jumble, so all nine letters are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Faltering means hesitating or wavering, as when someone is unsure.

clue.text: Get under someone's skin, as perfume?

blocks.note: first meaning, a verb stressed on the second syllable: to enrage
second meaning, a noun stressed on the first syllable: aromatic smoke

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently, which helps hide the shared spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense is to make very angry, and incense is a fragrant substance burnt for its scent.

clue.text: Stop voting system happening

blocks.note: PR is proportional representation
an event is a happening

explanation.surface: A call to halt an electoral method from coming into force.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to keep it from happening, so stop works as a verb synonym.
